features.label: WebRTC web API (RTCPeerConnection)

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Prevent GC of RTCDataChannel until its PeerConnection is GC-able.

patches.author: Keith Cirkel
patches.subject: Part 62 - Fixup final classes using _FINAL cycle collecting isupports macro in dom/media

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: move stats reports into WebrtcGlobalStatsHistory;r=bwc

features.summary: Firefox fixed memory management for WebRTC data channels to prevent them from being cleaned up prematurely, and reorganized how connection statistics are collected and tracked. _No visible user impact._

features.label: Camera & audio capture

patches.author: Nika Layzell
patches.subject: Part 1: Unify IPDL actor devirutalization logic, and require types to be fully qualified,

patches.author: serge-sans-paille
patches.subject: Cleanup default state for static-analysis on Windows / dom part

features.summary: Work on the camera and microphone capture plumbing focused on IPC and static-analysis hygiene. IPDL (the inter-process communication description language used for browser processes) actor devirtualization logic was unified so actor types are handled consistently and more efficiently, and Windows/dom default state was cleaned up for static analysis. These changes reduce build warnings and lower the risk of subtle cross-process capture bugs, helping make camera/audio capture more reliable.

features.label: libwebrtc integration

patches.author: Sylvestre Ledru
patches.subject: Fix unused function templates in dom/media to fix -Wunused-template with clang 23

patches.author: serge-sans-paille
patches.subject: Activate clang-tidy's modernize-use-transparent-functors check

features.summary: Maintenance and modernisation of the libwebrtc integration to keep builds clean on recent compilers: fixes for unused function templates to satisfy clang 23 and enabling a clang-tidy check (modernize-use-transparent-functors). This is build- and code-quality work that reduces warnings and makes future refactors safer; customers should see no direct behavioral change.

features.label: Session negotiation (SDP)

patches.author: Sylvestre Ledru
patches.subject: Restore ostream format state in SDP imageattr serialization (Coverity CID 1315812, 1315813, 1315814)

features.summary: A serialization fix for SDP (Session Description Protocol) image attributes ensures the stream formatting state is restored after writing. SDP is used during WebRTC session negotiation; restoring the ostream state prevents subtle formatting side effects that could break interoperability when browsers or endpoints exchange media capability information.

features.label: Video Engine

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2058388. Allow passing the DrawView flag to drawSnapshot so root scrollbars are painted, and so reftest's snapshot path matches its default one.

features.summary: _No visible change_—an internal improvement to Firefox's video rendering snapshot feature to better handle scrollbars during automated testing.

features.label: libwebrtc build

features.summary: Multiple WebRTC-related changes around codec selection, capability checks, and stats. MediaCapabilities queries and encoding paths now flow through asynchronous codec support, GMP (Gecko Media Plugins) codec creation is gated on plugin availability, H.264 profile-level info is placed correctly into codec parameters, hardware H.264 decode is retained when no software decoder is present, and WebRTC now reports rtxSsrc and retransmission statistics. Together these make video calls more compatible and reliable and provide better diagnostics for call quality — **improved retransmission and recovery reporting for WebRTC**.

features.summary: Common WebRTC plumbing improved: Firefox now fully supports extmap-allow-mixed (an RTP/RTCP header extension rule that allows mixing one-byte and two-byte extension formats), which makes header-extension handling more standards-compliant. The WebRTC port allowlist was exposed as a shared helper so different parts of the code use the same policy, and a small off-by-one bug in video stamping was fixed. Together these changes improve interoperability and internal correctness.

features.summary: Work on the camera and microphone capture plumbing focused on IPC and static-analysis hygiene. IPDL (the inter-process communication description language used for browser processes) actor devirtualization logic was unified so actor types are handled consistently and more efficiently, and Windows/dom default state was cleaned up for static analysis. These changes reduce build warnings and lower the risk of subtle cross-process capture bugs, helping make camera/audio capture more reliable.

features.summary: Recent updates to the negotiation engine in Firefox's JSEP (JavaScript Session Establishment Protocol) have improved how the browser handles errors related to SDP (Session Description Protocol) parsing. By introducing distinct error messages for parsing failures, developers can more easily identify and troubleshoot issues that arise during the establishment of multimedia sessions, such as video calls through WebRTC (the technology behind video calls). Additionally, applying `std::move` in various parts of the browser's code enhances performance by allowing the efficient transfer of data rather than duplicating it, leading to a smoother user experience without apparent _visible change_.

features.summary: Two fixes to SDP handling used in session negotiation: restoring ostream format state during imageattr serialization and a latent off-by-one bug fix. SDP (Session Description Protocol) is central to WebRTC call setup; these fixes prevent subtle serialization and indexing errors that could cause mis-negotiated media parameters or parsing failures, improving connection reliability.

features.label: WebRTC

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Implement RTCTransportStats.selectedCandidatePairChanges

features.summary: Recent updates to WebRTC, the technology behind video calls, have introduced the capability to track changes in selected candidate pairs for transport statistics. This means that developers can now better understand how their applications handle different network conditions by seeing which network routes (or candidates) are being selected during a call. The ability to monitor these changes is crucial for optimizing video and audio quality and ultimately enhances the user experience during live communications. **This improvement allows for more responsive handling of network fluctuations, making video calls smoother and more reliable.**
